name: Nova
behaviour: Asks a short follow-up question and pushes back once before accepting an explanation
learning_objectives: Get a revision on OOC you learnt in Year 1
Learn about Abstraction, Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Interfaces, and key differences between writing Simple Object Oriented Programs in C++ and Java

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Object Oriented programming is not a method of implementation
misconceptions.correct_concept: Object Oriented programming is a method of implementation in which programs are organized as cooperative collections of objects, each of which represents an instance of some class, and whose classes are all members of a hierarchy of classes united via inheritance relationships.
misconceptions.reason: Students may misunderstand the definition of Object Oriented programming and its role in software development.

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Object Oriented Programming is not a method of solving complex problems
misconceptions.correct_concept: Object Oriented Programming is a method of implementation in which programs are organized as a collection of objects which cooperate to solve a problem.
misconceptions.reason: Students may not recognize the benefits of using Object Oriented Programming to solve complex problems.

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Object Oriented Programming is not about developing complex systems using smaller subsystems
misconceptions.correct_concept: A complex system is developed using smaller subsystems, which are independent units containing their own data and functions, and can be reused to solve many different problems.
misconceptions.reason: Students may not understand the concept of subsystems and how they contribute to the development of complex systems.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of Object Oriented Programming?
options: To organize programs as cooperative collections of objects
To develop software using functional programming
To create complex systems using smaller subsystems
To solve complex problems using procedural programming
questions.explanation: Object Oriented Programming is a method of implementation in which programs are organized as cooperative collections of objects, each of which represents an instance of some class, and whose classes are all members of a hierarchy of classes united via inheritance relationships.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using Object Oriented Programming?
options: To develop software more quickly
To reuse code more effectively
To make code more readable
To solve complex problems more efficiently
questions.explanation: Object Oriented Programming is a method of implementation in which programs are organized as a collection of objects which cooperate to solve a problem.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using classes in Object Oriented Programming?
options: To develop software more quickly
To encapsulate data and behavior
To create complex systems using smaller subsystems
To reuse code more effectively
questions.explanation: A class is a blueprint for creating objects, which encapsulate data and behavior, and can be reused to solve many different problems.

questions.question: What is the primary way to reuse code in Object Oriented Programming?
options: By using inheritance
By creating objects
By using functions
By copying and pasting code
questions.explanation: Inheritance is the primary way to reuse code in Object Oriented Programming, where a child class inherits the properties and behavior of a parent class.

questions.question: What is the primary way to solve complex problems in Object Oriented Programming?
options: By using event-driven programming
By using functional programming
By using procedural programming
By using Object Oriented Programming
questions.explanation: Object Oriented Programming is a method of implementation in which programs are organized as a collection of objects which cooperate to solve a problem.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes Object Oriented Programming?
options: Object Oriented Programming is strictly limited to low-level assembly routines.
Object Oriented Programming is not about developing complex systems using smaller subsystems
Object Oriented Programming can only be instantiated once globally across an entire program.
A complex system is developed using smaller subsystems, which are independent units containing their own data and functions, and can be reused to solve many different problems.
